open_decisions.title: No mechanism enforces the frontier-then-crawls lock order, and StartCrawl takes it the other way round
open_decisions.authority: DECISIONS ADR-116 (round-2 observation 1); corrects ADR-105 in place
open_decisions.note: ADR-105 justified the checkpoint's lock order with "frontier THEN crawls is the subsystem's established order". TRUE OF `Admission#claim`, `CrawlDriver#retire` and `CrawlFetchDueSchedule.link_next`; FALSE OF `Handlers::StartCrawl`, which takes the `crawls` ROW lock in `store.start`'s compare-and-set (start_crawl.rb:275) and only then the frontier advisory lock in `Frontier#seed_roots` (:298). NO REACHABLE INTERLEAVING WAS DEMONSTRATED: a `crawl_terminal_deadline` action for a Crawl cannot exist until that same StartCrawl transaction commits, and a redelivered StartCrawl refuses before the compare-and-set — so this is a latent hazard, not a live defect, and it is why ADR-113 deliberately takes a PLAIN SELECT on `crawls` inside `retire` rather than a row lock. WHAT IS MISSING is any mechanism that would catch a future writer taking the two the other way round; the claim was load-bearing for a repair and was checked by nobody. RECOMMENDED: either reorder `StartCrawl` so all four writers agree (it seeds the frontier after the CAS, so the frontier lock could be taken first), or an architecture-fitness check over the two lock objects. Related in kind to FU-7, which recommends the same shape of mechanical check for :128. RESOLVED 2026-08-03 (round 4, R4-2). THE 'LATENT, NOT LIVE' JUSTIFICATION WAS INVALIDATED BY R3-6 AND THIS ITEM WAS WRONGLY CARRIED AS 'open and unchanged'. That justification -- 'no reachable interleaving exists, because a crawl_terminal_deadline action cannot exist until that StartCrawl transaction commits' -- covers `CompleteCrawl` and nothing else. R3-6 made `Handlers::CancelCrawl` take the frontier lock first, and a cancellation is a CUSTOMER COMMAND that depends on no prior commit; :736 makes a `queued` Crawl cancellable, so cancelling one while the dispatcher starts it is an ordinary race. StartCrawl held the `crawls` ROW (`store.start`, a bare UPDATE) and then waited on `crawl-frontier`, while CancelCrawl held `crawl-frontier` and waited on the row: a cycle, resolved by PostgreSQL aborting one side with SQLSTATE 40P01, and `Handlers::CancelCrawl` contains ZERO rescue clauses so it would surface as a raw `PG::TRDeadlockDetected` instead of a `Platform::CommandResult`. THE REPAIR: `StartCrawl#accept` now takes `lock_frontier` immediately before `store.start`, so the whole subsystem is frontier-then-crawls with no exception. Placed there and not earlier because `command_executions` and `entitlement_reservations` carry no FK to `crawls` (checked against pg_constraint), so nothing above it holds even a FOR KEY SHARE -- which is also what keeps PROOF 88's window intact. PROVED by PROOF 126, which suspends the start between `store.start` and `seed_roots` via a trigger on `evaluations` and asserts the cancellation queues on the FRONTIER; under the reverted fix it queues on the row instead and the example names the cycle.

open_decisions.title: Preflight's no-working-state policy is proven only against synthetic fixtures and never runs against the real BUILD_STATE
open_decisions.authority: Found while repairing the live record: status was left at the WORKING token `implementing` after the run had exited, which AUTONOMOUS_BUILD_CONTROLLER forbids
open_decisions.note: `AutonomousBuild::Preflight` DOES implement the invariant — `spec/automation/policy/preflight_spec.rb:53` proves it fails a build state whose status is `implementing` — but every assertion in that file builds a synthetic `BuildState` in a `Dir.mktmpdir` repository. NOTHING APPLIES THE POLICY TO `specification/automation/BUILD_STATE.json`, so the real record sat in a WORKING state across two full review rounds and neither round named it. THE OBVIOUS FIX IS WRONG: a blanket "status is never WORKING" assertion in `spec/architecture/repository_truth_spec.rb` would fire during a legitimate controller run, when `implementing` on disk is the correct value — the suite is itself a gate the controller runs mid-run. WHAT IS ACTUALLY BROKEN is that the working-state token is only illegal AT A RUN BOUNDARY, and no boundary check reads the real file. RECOMMENDED: run `Preflight.check` against the real BUILD_STATE from `bin/autonomous-build` (or an equivalent boundary hook) rather than widening the always-on truth spec, so the invariant is enforced where it is true instead of where it is convenient. Same shape as FU-38 and FU-7: a load-bearing claim with no mechanism behind it.

open_decisions.title: Six failed acceptance rounds are carried outside failed_attempts, which is empty and has no production writer
open_decisions.authority: ADR-118 authoritative-state reconciliation: attempt_number is 6 and failed_attempts is [] after six five-lens rounds returned NOT ACCEPTED
open_decisions.note: `failed_attempts` is a REQUIRED, VALIDATED, append-only-in-intent field with a dedicated `append_failed_attempt` writer, but its only repository caller is its unit spec. No controller path writes it, so it remains structurally incapable of recording a failed review. Six failures are real: rounds 1 through 6 all returned NOT ACCEPTED, and their findings remain in `S-07-009_ACCEPTANCE_REVIEW.md` and the state reconciliation rather than in this structured field. A reader that trusts only `failed_attempts` still concludes the tranche has never failed. RECOMMENDED: define the record shape explicitly, backfill all six outcomes and call `append_failed_attempt` from the review-failure transition. NOT DONE HERE because recording ADR-118 does not authorize a shape-defining controller change; this reconciliation corrects the stale count without inventing that schema. RESOLVED 2026-08-10 (ADR-145), AND THE COUNT IN THIS NOTE WAS WRONG. `failed_attempts` now has a declared shape -- BuildState::FAILED_ATTEMPT_KEYS: attempt, tranche, candidate_range, outcome, mechanism, blocking_findings, record -- with a closed outcome enumeration, a pinned base..head check that refuses `..HEAD`, and validation on LOAD as well as on APPEND so a hand-edited row is checked like any other. THE BACKFILL IS FOURTEEN, NOT SIX: S-07-009_ACCEPTANCE_REVIEW.md carries fourteen round headings and every one records 'VERDICT: FAIL ... NOT ACCEPTED'; six was true when this note was written and stale by the time it was read. Each row carries the candidate range its own section pins and the blocking-finding count its own verdict states. NOT RECONCILED: ADR-142's prose says 'eighteen recorded five-lens rounds', numbered on a different scheme from the headings; fourteen is what the repository holds as per-round evidence and is what is recorded, and the discrepancy is named rather than overwritten. TWO GATES IN repository_truth_spec DERIVE the set from every *_ACCEPTANCE_REVIEW.md rather than restating it, so a fifteenth unrecorded failed round fails the run. A LATENT CONTROLLER DEFECT WAS FOUND BY WRITING THE FIRST PROOF: `do_review` wrote a fixed `review.json` into an APPEND-ONLY run record, so the SECOND review in a run -- the only kind that exists after `changes_required` -- raised 'run-record artifact already exists' out of `run_tranche`, which does not rescue it. The review-failure loop-back had therefore never once completed, which is the deeper reason this field stayed empty. The artifact is now numbered by repair cycle and `append_failed_attempt` is called from that branch, with a `failed_attempt_not_recorded` event rather than a silent swallow if the write fails.

open_decisions.title: After R3-6, lock_crawl's FOR UPDATE is superseded by the frontier advisory lock and is asserted by nothing
open_decisions.authority: Found by mutation while repairing R3-6; the repair itself created it
open_decisions.note: R3-6 made `Handlers::CancelCrawl` take `lock_frontier` before `lock_crawl`, matching `CompleteCrawl`, `retire` and `Admission#claim`. `lock_crawl` has EXACTLY TWO CALLERS (`complete_crawl.rb:118`, `cancel_crawl.rb:118`) and both now hold the transaction-scoped advisory lock `crawl-frontier:<crawl_id>` first, so for one Crawl they are ALREADY mutually exclusive before the row lock is taken. MEASURED: before R3-6, deleting `FOR UPDATE` from `crawl_start_store.rb`'s `lock_crawl` failed PROOF 100 and 101; after R3-6 it leaves the WHOLE SUITE GREEN at 2070/0. This is the R3-5 defect class -- a control asserted by nothing -- REINTRODUCED BY A REPAIR, which is the third time in this tranche that a fix has created an evidence hole (round 2 found two in round 1's repairs). THE FOR UPDATE WAS DELIBERATELY RETAINED, not removed: ADR-105 takes both locks by design and removing a lock on the strength of 'the other one covers it' is how the next inversion becomes unreachable to review. WHAT IS MISSING is any test that can distinguish its presence. A structural assertion that the SQL contains the words would be exactly the vacuous evidence this repository rejects. RECOMMENDED: either demonstrate a reachable race the advisory lock does not cover and pin it, or record the redundancy explicitly in ADR-105 so a later reader does not mistake an unassertable control for a tested one. Same shape as FU-38, FU-39 and FU-40: a load-bearing claim with no mechanism behind it. REFUTED AND CLOSED 2026-08-03 (round 4). THE REASONING IN THIS NOTE IS WRONG. `lock_crawl` has two callers, but the `crawls` ROW has a THIRD WRITER that takes no frontier lock: `CrawlStartStore#start` and `#fail`, from `Handlers::StartCrawl`. So `FOR UPDATE` was never 'superseded by the frontier lock' -- with it, a cancellation racing an in-flight start blocks, re-reads and answers `stale_state_version`; without it, it reads the pre-image, passes both guards, matches zero rows and raises `Platform::InvariantViolation` ('crawl cancellation lost its serialized transition'). Retaining it was right, and this record as written would have licensed removing a load-bearing control -- which is the more dangerous half of the error. The measurement that prompted the note (deleting FOR UPDATE leaves the suite green) remains true and is now explained: the suite had no example entering the StartCrawl window, which is the same gap R4-2 closed. THE ROUND-4 REPAIR ALSO CHANGES THE PREMISE: `StartCrawl` now takes the frontier lock before `store.start`, so all three writers hold it first.

open_decisions.title: Spec-level constants land on Object, so two spec files can silently read each other's document
open_decisions.authority: Found while building the R3-10 transcription check; reproduced, then avoided rather than fixed
open_decisions.note: A constant assigned inside an `RSpec.describe ... do` block is defined in the enclosing LEXICAL scope, which is top level -- NOT on the example group. `spec/architecture/scheduled_action_catalogue_spec.rb:16` defines `DOC = .../BACKGROUND_PROCESSING.md` this way. The first draft of `spec/architecture/permission_baseline_transcription_spec.rb` defined its own `DOC = .../WORKFLOW_SPECIFICATIONS.md`, and IN THE SUITE it read BACKGROUND_PROCESSING.md instead: green when run alone, failing when run with the directory, and which value wins is decided purely by RSpec's load order. It was caught only because that spec asserts its own parse before using it -- a file WITHOUT such a guard would have parsed zero rows from the wrong document and passed every derived example VACUOUSLY, which is the exact R3-8/R3-9 defect class arriving through a new door. THE NEW FILE AVOIDS IT by using methods instead of constants; the LANDMINE IS UNCHANGED, because `scheduled_action_catalogue_spec.rb` still owns a top-level `DOC` and the next spec to declare one collides with it. RECOMMENDED: a cheap architecture check that fails when two spec files assign the same top-level constant, or a convention (enforced, not written down) that spec-level shared values are methods or `let`. NOT DONE HERE because it is a repository-wide test-infrastructure convention rather than an S-07-009 defect, and this tranche is already carrying three evidence-hole follow-ups. Sibling of FU-38/39/40/41: a claim that holds only by an accident nothing checks. RESOLVED 2026-08-09 by the check this record asked for: spec/architecture/spec_constant_scope_spec.rb walks every spec file with Prism and fails the run when two files write the SAME top-level constant. It walks the AST rather than grepping text, so a constant inside `class` or `module` - properly namespaced, not a collision - is correctly ignored, and only assignments whose enclosing scope is the file root are collected. IT FOUND A LIVE COLLISION THE RECORD DID NOT KNOW ABOUT, on its first run: `ROBOTS_ALLOW_ALL` was written at describe level by BOTH spec/acceptance/wf005_document_ingestion_spec.rb and spec/acceptance/wf005_record_fetch_attempt_spec.rb. HARMLESS TODAY AND ONLY BY LUCK - the two values are byte-identical, so whichever load order won produced the same string; a change to either file would have silently changed the other. The second file's own note at the foot of it already called this 'the same hazard already in the file'. ONE SIDE WAS CONVERTED TO A METHOD, NOT BOTH, AND THE REASON IS RECORDED RATHER THAN GLOSSED: `wf005_document_ingestion_spec.rb` is bound by 120 rows of S-07-010_MUTATION_LEDGER.json which record their killed examples by FILE:LINE, so inserting even a comment there makes the ledger describe a proof that no longer exists - measured, not predicted: the first attempt did exactly that and `repository_truth_spec` :541 failed with 'the proof that failed is not the proof that exists'. Re-sealing means replaying the mutations, not editing a digest, so the touch was reverted instead. A collision needs TWO writers, so removing one ends it, and the check now fails the run if a second ever reappears. NOT CLAIMED: this catches COLLISIONS, not the single-file case where a spec-level constant merely leaks onto `Object` without anything else declaring it; that remains legal and is what the convention, not the check, addresses.

open_decisions.title: BLOCKED ON AN OWNER DECISION (R3-4 half a): F-01 re-arms `timeout_s` per REDIRECT HOP, so a wall-clock-bounded request can overrun 11.1x
open_decisions.authority: ADR-141. Owner decision of 2026-08-06 ratifying the FOUNDATION-001 evolution, requiring the total deadline as the authoritative correction and explicitly declining both the lower-redirect mitigation and any documentation of the overrun as accepted behaviour
open_decisions.note: RESOLVED 2026-08-06 by ADR-141, under the OWNER'S RATIFICATION of the frozen-contract evolution (FOUNDATION-001 property 6a). Half (b) was repaired at round 3; HALF (a) COULD NOT BE REPAIRED BY ANY CALLER, because the facade accepted only a PER-ATTEMPT number and `GuardedHttpClient#attempt` re-armed it at every redirect hop for both the resolver call and the connect/read deadline -- 11.1x measured at the ratified 10-redirect ceiling, up to 22x with DNS. ONE `fetch` NOW HAS ONE WALL-CLOCK BOUNDARY: DNS, connect, TLS, headers, body and every hop spend it, no hop re-arms anything, and exhaustion stops the client deterministically with the ratified `:timeout` outcome. The per-attempt timeout survives only as a SUBORDINATE CEILING -- every operation asks `effective_timeout_s(remaining)` = `[timeout_s, remaining].min`, one place, so no operation can be handed a budget the total does not have. The total is clamped to the SAME 15s hard bound as the per-attempt ceiling, so the overrun is arithmetically impossible rather than discouraged. `total_timeout_s` DEFAULTS TO `timeout_s`, so omitting it is the TIGHTEST form and no shape of the call is unbounded -- the owner's sixth requirement. EVIDENCE is a MAXIMUM-LENGTH CHAIN measured on the wall clock (`spec/platform/outbound/total_deadline_spec.rb`): the chain completes under a sufficient budget; under an insufficient one it is `:timeout`, opens FEWER than eleven connections, never reaches the terminal host, and finishes within the budget plus one hop. Five mutations restore one limb each and ALL FIVE DIE. TWO SURVIVED THE FIRST DRAFT AND BOTH WERE GAPS IN THE PROOF, NOT THE CODE: the harness burned its time in the resolver so the connect/read cap was bound by nothing, and deleting the pre-hop budget check left the OUTCOME identical while still consulting the CALLER'S `redirect_guard` -- :448's robots and Source Scope recheck, which takes a lock and writes an authorization decision -- for a hop that can never be made. The connector now records the absolute deadline it is handed and the guard records its invocations. THREE STALE ARITHMETIC CLAIMS CORRECTED where they stand (~165s in Lease and EnsureRobots, ~330s in DiscoverSitemaps); the renewal boundaries they justify are unchanged and still correct. BEHAVIOUR IS STRICTLY TIGHTER EVERYWHERE: a single-attempt request that had `timeout_s` for DNS AND `timeout_s` for connect+response now has one budget covering both.

open_decisions.title: WORKFLOW :551's equality boundary in Platform::Entitlement::Service#commit is not pinned by a falsifiable proof
open_decisions.authority: ADR-124 (round-9 repair authority): re-derived from clean evidence and SUPERSEDED
open_decisions.note: SUPERSEDED 2026-08-04 as an ERRONEOUS FOLLOW-UP RECORD, with the reason recorded rather than the record deleted. FU-44 stated that the round-7 boundary example does not kill the `>=` -> `>` mutation at `Entitlement::Service#commit` and that the reason was undiagnosed. The reason is now diagnosed and the premise is false: `app/platform/entitlement/service.rb` holds THREE identical `if now >= effective_deadline(r)` comparisons (:113 start_execution, :130 heartbeat, :150 commit), so an UNSCOPED substitution lands on the FIRST of them and never reaches the site FU-44 names. With the mutation applied AT :150 and CONFIRMED LANDED BY DIFF, `spec/platform/entitlement/service_spec.rb`'s boundary example fails deterministically -- round 8 reproduced this three times out of three and round 9 a fourth. A DIFFERENT AND REAL SURVIVOR WAS FOUND IN ITS PLACE: :113's prestart boundary genuinely survived the entire entitlement suite, and is now closed by a named boundary example that kills it 3/3 (`fu44b-start-execution-ge-to-gt` in the mutation ledger). NO F-05 IMPLEMENTATION WAS CHANGED to preserve this follow-up's existence; the change is one test-only example that closes a demonstrated gap.

RESOLVED 2026-08-05 on repair/s07-009-r12. Both mandatory checks now have real, owned targets and both execute. `spec/automation/locking` holds controller_lock_spec.rb: one holder at a time, a second acquirer REFUSED rather than queued (bounded, so a blocking implementation fails), release, and the kernel releasing the lock when a real forked holder is SIGKILLed. `spec/automation/crash_recovery` holds build_state_crash_spec.rb, which had NO coverage anywhere: a real child process is killed mid-write-loop and the state file must remain complete, parseable, loadable by the controller's own reader and free of stranded temporaries; the crashed run's lock must be reclaimable exactly once; and an invalid update must be refused BEFORE it lands, so a bad write cannot be blamed on a crash. All waits are bounded and report what was still held. `spec/architecture/mandatory_gate_targets_spec.rb` makes the declaration itself the thing under test: every mandatory gate's target must exist and define at least one example, or a bin/ target must exist and be executable. Verified adversarially by removing both new directories, which fails it by name. No mandatory declaration was deleted or weakened.

The repository's root .gitignore exists on disk but is UNTRACKED, because this machine's global ignore file (~/.gitignore_global:6) ignores every .gitignore. `git worktree add` materialises only tracked files, so every linked worktree starts with NO ignore rules and `git add -A` sweeps in tmp/, log/, .bundle/ and config/master.key. This actually happened twice during the S-07-009 and PREREQ-DB-BOOTSTRAP work; neither branch was pushed and origin has never held the key. The hazard is closed for existing and future worktrees via the shared info/exclude, which is NOT versioned. The durable fix is an owner decision because it interacts with a global setting: either force-track a root .gitignore (`git add -f .gitignore`) or remove `.gitignore` from the global ignore file. Recorded by ADR-130.

BUILD_STATE.current_tranche is load-bearing in a way its name does not advertise: spec/architecture/repository_truth_spec.rb derives six checks from it, and writing a value that is not a tranche identifier (PREREQ-DB-BOOTSTRAP was written there once during this work) makes all six pass vacuously instead of failing. An invalid identifier must FAIL LOUDLY. Resolve by validating current_tranche against BUILD_PLAN's known tranche identifiers and failing when it does not resolve, and by applying the same rule to any other field a gate silently derives its subject from. Recorded by ADR-130.

RESOLVED 2026-08-05 on repair/s07-009-d7 under the D7 owner decision, recorded by ADR-132. The capability axis is now a CONJUNCT of every protected write: each of the three statements carries `IdentityAccess::Authorization::WriteAuthority` -- the granting Role Assignments the decision relied on, with their state versions and scope digests -- and PostgreSQL re-reads them under FOR SHARE in the same statement as the transition. An actor who never held the capability carries no grant, so the array is empty and the predicate is false. The SCOPE limb this record demonstrated (removing `authorized_for_scope?`'s single operand let a MarketingOperator commit an ORGANIZATION-scope policy through 2364 examples) is closed by carrying the role the ratified :732/:738 scope rule demands into the statement as `required_role`; `ActivateCrawlPolicy::SCOPE_ROLE` is the one transcription both the Ruby guard and the write read. `AuthorityAttestation` carries the same object, so an attestation minted for one capability, grant set or scope rule cannot be presented at a write carrying another. Observable by the same proof system: PROOF 243-258c, and the sentinel's antecedent is now :335's protected side effect rather than any write. WHAT IS NOT DECIDED HERE: Assignment-scope CONTAINMENT against the target remains FU-2, a pre-existing platform-wide deferral under ADR-066; inventing it under a repair would be new authorization semantics. The axis now has a place at the write for that predicate to attach to.

open_decisions.title: the scope-containment predicate now has a home at the write, and FU-2 must fill it
open_decisions.authority: DECISIONS ADR-132 (D7); FU-2 under ADR-066
open_decisions.note: D7 gave the scope axis a write-level representation: `WriteAuthority` carries the grant's scope digest and the role the ratified scope rule demands, and the capability CTE binds both. It does NOT implement Assignment-scope CONTAINMENT against the target, which is FU-2's platform-wide question and not an S-07-009 one. When FU-2 is taken, the containment predicate belongs in that CTE beside the bindings D7 added, rather than in a fourth Ruby guard. Recorded so the next tranche does not re-derive where it goes.

open_decisions.title: The capability CTE is still written three times
open_decisions.authority: Round-15 architecture finding A15-1 (ADR-133)
open_decisions.note: AMENDED 2026-08-06 (round 19, finding R19-CTR-2). THE ORIGINAL NOTE'S BASIS WAS FALSE. It read 'the round-15 battery makes the three copies provably agree -- any drift fails seven cases at the drifting write -- so this is a duplication, not a live risk'. MEASURED: replacing `ra.account_id = $n::uuid` with a same-arity tautology left all 27 battery examples green, and across the whole 2464-example suite the only thing that reacted was `repository_truth_spec`'s mutation-applicability check -- a byte-digest staleness test that produces the IDENTICAL failure for a comment-only edit. Nothing in the suite could distinguish deleting an authorization qual from adding a comment. Six single-qual drifts were tried; only `FOR SHARE OF ra` was caught. REPAIRED IN PART: round 19 added a shared-example case binding the PRINCIPAL conjunct at all three writes (verified to fail at exactly the drifting write, independently at each), and ledger definition `r19-account-qual-unbound`. WHAT REMAINS: the organization limb is still unproved, and R19-ARCH-3 showed the copies agree in SQL TEXT while ALREADY DIFFERING in the operand bound to the organization slot -- `crawl_store`/`crawl_policy_store` bind the ROW's id, `crawl_start_store` binds the AUTHORITY's -- which a textual comparison cannot see. The architecture lens's reasoned verdict is that EXTRACTION IS THE WRONG REPAIR: the predicate is safe because it is a conjunct of the statement with nothing to hoist, and a shared fragment interpolated into three statements moves back toward the rule-split-across-writers shape ADR-095 records. The right repair is one architecture spec asserting the three CTEs are equivalent under placeholder normalisation AND that each binds the same semantic value into the organization slot. ROUND-20 MEASUREMENT (finding F-3), which sharpens what remains: a per-qual attribution matrix of 30 same-arity tautologies (10 conjuncts x 3 writes) shows every conjunct killing the same named example at each write — no case is vacuous at one write while meaningful at another. TWO CONJUNCTS KILL NOTHING IN THE BATTERY. `required_role` at the policy write is bound outside it (PROOF 258) and is genuinely inert at the other two, where production passes none. `ra.organization_id` IS UNBOUND ACROSS THE ENTIRE 2472-EXAMPLE SUITE at all three writes — the only reaction is `repository_truth_spec`'s byte-digest staleness check, which fires identically for a comment-only edit. That is the organization limb this note already records as unproved, now measured against the whole suite rather than the battery alone. REPAIRED IN PART 2026-08-10, ALONG THE LINE THIS NOTE'S ARCHITECTURE LENS ARGUED FOR, AND NOT BY EXTRACTION. `spec/architecture/capability_cte_equivalence_spec.rb` takes each protected write's `capability_authority` CTE by balanced parentheses, strips comments, normalises `$n` to `$?` and compares the three as CONJUNCT MULTISETS, plus the pre-WHERE shape and the `FOR SHARE OF ra` lock separately. MEASURED: comment-stripped and placeholder-normalised, `CrawlStartStore#cancel` and `CrawlStore#insert_crawl` are BYTE-IDENTICAL, and `CrawlPolicyStore#activate_version` differs only in WHERE the `required_role` conjunct sits in the AND chain — so the three already agree, and the gate records that agreement rather than creating it. The comparison subject is `ProtectedWrites.covered`, the registry FU-61's completeness gate proves against the repository, so a fourth protected write joins this comparison when it is registered instead of being compared against nothing. MEASURED AGAINST THIS NOTE'S OWN BLIND SPOT, SERIALLY AND ALONE: substituting a same-arity tautology for the `required_role` conjunct AT THE QUEUE WRITE ONLY leaves the battery at 69 examples / 0 failures — reproducing exactly what round 20 recorded — and fails the new gate, naming the conjunct and both writes. That closes the class this note describes: a conjunct dropped or weakened at ONE write and left at the others is invisible to a per-write proof and visible here immediately, including for the two conjuncts round 20's attribution matrix found bound by nothing at all. WHAT REMAINS OPEN, AND IT IS THE HALF THIS NOTE CALLS R19-ARCH-3. The gate proves the three PREDICATES agree; it cannot prove they bind the same OPERAND, because after normalisation every binding is `$?`. Re-measured at the call sites: `CrawlStartStore#cancel` binds `authority.organization_id` into `ra.organization_id`, while `CrawlPolicyStore#activate_version` and `CrawlStore#insert_crawl` bind `row[:organization_id]` — the divergence this note already records, still live, still invisible to any textual comparison. IT WAS NOT REPAIRED HERE BECAUSE THE REPAIR IS A CHOICE, NOT A RECONCILIATION: making all three bind `authority.organization_id` is the safer direction, since that value is derived from the authenticated Session and never from caller input, but it is a behaviour change in the authority layer at two accepted writes and this note's own standard is to prove such a change rather than assume it. It wants its own measured tranche, in the shape the equivalence gate above now makes checkable. RE-MEASURED 2026-08-10 (approval-switch tranche), AND THE DIVERGENCE IS TEXTUAL RATHER THAN SEMANTIC AT EVERY CALL SITE TODAY. Traced all three: `Handlers::QueueCrawl#commit` and `Handlers::ActivateCrawlPolicy` both set `org = actor.organization_id` and build their authority with `WriteAuthority.for(actor:, ...)`, whose `organization_id` IS `actor.organization_id`, so `row[:organization_id]` and `authority.organization_id` are THE SAME VALUE at both writes; `Handlers::CancelCrawl` passes `authority:` alone and the store already binds `authority.organization_id`. So the three CTEs agree in operand as well as in predicate at present, and unifying them changes no behaviour reachable today. WHAT IS ACTUALLY UNPROVED IS THEREFORE NARROWER THAN THIS NOTE SAID: not that the writes disagree, but that NOTHING ENFORCES their agreement — a future caller passing a `row[:organization_id]` other than the authenticated one would have the capability CTE look for grants in the CALLER-SUPPLIED organization, and no spec, guard or gate would notice. The exact repair is one of: bind `authority.organization_id` into the CTE's organization slot at the two row-bound writes (behaviour-preserving today, by the trace above), or refuse the divergence outright in the store. It is STILL NOT TAKEN HERE, on this note's own standard: both are changes in the authority layer at two accepted writes, and the proof that distinguishes them needs a cross-organization grant fixture that does not exist yet. The measurement above is what that tranche should start from. RESOLVED 2026-08-10 BY OWNER DECISION (ADR-145). All three protected writes now bind `authority.organization_id` into BOTH authority limbs: `CrawlStartStore#cancel` always did, and `CrawlStore#insert_crawl` and `CrawlPolicyStore#activate_version` each carry a new parameter for it while the row's organization stays the value INSERTED and the scope the supersession selects. THE REBINDING ALONE WOULD HAVE MOVED THE HAZARD RATHER THAN REMOVED IT, which is why the store also refuses the divergence: after rebinding, a caller passing a foreign row organization would have had the authority limbs answer about the AUTHENTICATED Organization while the row carried another, leaving `crawls_context` / `crawl_policies_context` to refuse the write -- an RLS error from the database instead of a broken contract at the store. `WriteAuthority#governs!` refuses before the statement, raising Platform::InvariantViolation and naming both organizations. Nothing reachable today changes, which is why it needed proving rather than assuming. THE TWO HALVES CANNOT BE PROVED THE SAME WAY and each has its own proof: the REFUSAL by execution against a real second Organization bootstrapped through the real WF-001 chain (spec/acceptance/wf005_write_authority_organization_spec.rb, 5 examples, 2 of them non-vacuity controls that must still commit), the BINDING by spec/architecture/capability_cte_equivalence_spec.rb, which resolves each store's organization placeholders back through its own parameter list -- because a behavioural binding proof needs the two values to differ and the refusal makes that unreachable. MEASURED: rebinding the queue write's capability CTE to `$4` fails the operand gate naming the write and the expression `row[:organization_id]`; deleting the queue write's `governs!` fails exactly one acceptance example and the policy write's exactly two. This closes R19-ARCH-3, the half the existing equivalence gate structurally cannot see because it normalises every `$n` to `$?`.

open_decisions.title: ProtectedEffectDoor's 42601 branch records nothing
open_decisions.authority: Round-15 schema observation O-3 (ADR-133)
open_decisions.note: AMENDED 2026-08-06 (round 19, findings R19-SCHEMA-2 and R19-SCHEMA-3). THE STATED JUSTIFICATION IS FALSE, THOUGH THE CONCLUSION STILL HOLDS. The door's comment says a 42601 statement 'carries no ModifyTable, so the absence of a plan is the correct answer rather than a blind spot'. `EXPLAIN` accepts only `ExplainableStmt`, and several statements outside that production DO modify tables. Reproduced through the door's own plan path: TRUNCATE, `COPY ... FROM STDIN`, CALL and `DO $$..$$` are all SWALLOWED_AS_NO_WRITE, and the COPY case demonstrably wrote 2 rows while the door returned []. A sweep of app/ and lib/ finds zero such production statements, so the corpus conclusion stands and this is NON-BLOCKING. SECOND INSTANCE, SAME CLASS, AND THIS ONE HAS A LIVE CALL SITE (R19-SCHEMA-3): the door is equally blind to DML inside SECURITY DEFINER plpgsql. Fifteen volatile SECURITY DEFINER functions perform DML and `f1_settle_scheduled_action` is called from `record_fetch_attempt.rb`; not exploitable against AuthoritySentinel because that path is a service delivery so the human-authorized antecedent is false. REPAIR: stop inferring 'no write' from the absence of a plan. `GovernedWriteSentinel` already holds the executed `PG::Result`, and PostgreSQL's own command tag (`cmd_status` -> 'COPY 2', 'TRUNCATE TABLE', 'MERGE ...') answers 'did this modify a relation' without a regex. NOT ATTEMPTED 2026-08-09, and the reason is scope rather than doubt. TWO THINGS WERE MEASURED THIS SESSION AND ARE RECORDED SO THE NEXT IMPLEMENTER DOES NOT RE-DERIVE THEM. (1) The blind spot reproduces exactly as stated: `EXPLAIN (GENERIC_PLAN, FORMAT JSON) TRUNCATE crawl_host_gates` fails with SQLSTATE 42601, so `ProtectedEffectDoor.plan` takes its `SYNTAX_ERROR` limb at spec/support/protected_effect_door.rb :121 and returns `[]` - 'no write' - for a statement that empties a governed table. (2) The command tags the repair would rely on, measured against PostgreSQL 17: TRUNCATE -> 'TRUNCATE TABLE'; COPY ... FROM STDIN -> 'COPY 1'; DO $$..$$ -> 'DO'; and the benign ones BEGIN -> 'BEGIN', COMMIT -> 'COMMIT', SET -> 'SET', CREATE INDEX -> 'CREATE INDEX'. WHAT MAKES IT LARGER THAN IT LOOKS: `cmd_status` names the VERB and never the RELATION, so a TRUNCATE can only ever be recorded as an instrument BLIND SPOT (`note_unplannable`, which fails the run) and never as an Effect with a relation - which is the correct outcome and should be stated in the repair rather than discovered during it. The classification also happens BEFORE execution (spec/support/authority_sentinel.rb :373-376 plans, then calls `super`), so the result carrying the tag arrives after the decision is made and the door needs a second entry point taking the tag. Finally the repair requires a judgement about which command tags are benign, and getting that allowlist wrong turns ordinary harness DDL into run-failing blind spots. That is a change to the instrument every spec in the suite runs behind, and it deserves its own validated tranche rather than the tail of another one.

open_decisions.title: The write's capability limb is a grant-identity limb, not a capability limb
open_decisions.authority: Round-15 security observation O1 (ADR-133)
open_decisions.note: WriteAuthority#capability is compared in Ruby by same_principal? and is bound into no statement. The SQL asks whether the grant the decision named is still the grant it named; it does not ask whether that grant CONFERS the capability. With the baseline confers? check neutralised (base code, out of range) a SecurityOperator queued and cancelled a Crawl; ActivateCrawlPolicy survived only because required_role gives that one write a role axis. Repair consistent with ADR-132's no-second-copy ruling: derive a required-role set from the single Ruby transcription and pass it for all three capabilities as SCOPE_ROLE already is. RESOLVED 2026-08-06 by ADR-135 (round-17 finding R17-SEC-1): `WriteAuthority` now carries `allowed_roles` — the ratified PermissionBaseline cell, read once in Ruby, immutable for the life of a deploy — and every protected write binds `AND ra.canonical_role = ANY($n::text[])`. The battery gains the case at all three writes and three mutations bind it.

open_decisions.title: Two protected writes judge authority against the row's organization_id, the third against the authority's
open_decisions.authority: Round-16 security observation O2 (ADR-134)
open_decisions.note: AMENDED 2026-08-06 (round 19, findings R19-SEC-4 and R19-SCHEMA-1). MEASURED FROM BOTH SIDES, and the divergence is real in both directions while the composite fails closed. SECURITY LENS: `crawl_start_store#cancel` binds both CTEs to `authority.organization_id` while its `UPDATE crawls ... WHERE id = $1::uuid` carries NO organization predicate; driven with a real attacker session against a victim organization's running Crawl, BOTH authority limbs returned authorized (`epoch_authorized: true, capability_authorized: true`) and only RLS stopped the write (`moved: 0`). SCHEMA LENS: the mirror in `crawl_store#insert_crawl`, which binds the ROW's org -- an org-B authority against an org-A row returned `epoch_authorized: true`, failing closed only via the capability CTE, and `role_assignments` has NO foreign keys at all, so that consistency is a WF-013 guarantee rather than a database one. UNREACHABLE from any built handler: `queue_crawl.rb`, `activate_crawl_policy.rb` and `cancel_crawl.rb` all derive org from the authenticated actor. NON-BLOCKING. The repair is still the one recorded: bind all three to the AUTHORITY's organization and add `AND organization_id = $n::uuid` to cancel's UPDATE target, so each store holds its own contract rather than depending on the one caller that derives the id correctly -- which is the principle `crawl_policy_store.rb:135` already ratified. RESOLVED 2026-08-10 (ADR-147), AND HALF OF THIS NOTE WAS ALREADY STALE WHEN IT WAS READ. The MIRROR it records at `crawl_store#insert_crawl` -- 'binds the ROW's org' -- was closed by FU-50 on 2026-08-10 (ADR-145): both row-bound writes now bind `authority.organization_id` into both authority limbs and refuse a divergent row organization via `WriteAuthority#governs!`. What remained is the half this note names first, and FU-50 did NOT close it: `cancel` takes an id rather than a row, so there was nothing for `governs!` to refuse, and its `UPDATE crawls` still carried no organization predicate. IT NOW CARRIES `AND organization_id = $5::uuid`, bound to the AUTHORITY's organization -- the same answer FU-50 settled at the other two, and the principle `crawl_policy_store.rb` already ratified for the superseded row. PROVED THE WAY THIS NOTE'S OWN MEASUREMENT COULD NOT BE: round 19 recorded 'only RLS stopped the write', which is an observation about the database's policy rather than about the statement. Driven on `DbInspector`'s BYPASSRLS superuser connection -- which the harness already relies on for cross-principal reads -- the policy is not there to stop it, and against the pre-change code a valid attacker authority CANCELLED a victim Organization's running Crawl (`epoch_authorized: true, capability_authorized: true, moved: 1`), irreversibly, because `f1_crawls_guard` refuses every edge out of a terminal state. With the predicate, `moved: 0` and the Crawl stays running; the legitimate same-Organization cancellation on the same connection still applies, which is what stops the example passing because the statement refuses everything.

The directive's Tier 1 rule governs authorization defects and its owner-interaction threshold is not met: `:335` resolves the specification question outright, the change strengthens authorization, and no frozen contract is touched. AUTONOMY_POLICY's 'not another tranche's backlog' limit is what had held this as owner_decision_required

THREE MUTATIONS, ALL KILLED: `fu54-protected-entitlement-entry-deleted` (3 failures), `fu54-protected-close-arm-widened` (1), `fu54-protected-investigation-entry-deleted` (1) -- the same deletions that left the suite green before. ONE FIXTURE encoded a classification it does not own (`wf013_activation_lifecycle_spec` seeded BillingOperator among three roles and asserted three activation timers); its roles and expected count are now derived, and the invariant under test is unchanged. CUSTOMER-VISIBLE CONSEQUENCE: a BillingOperator grant now requires approval by a different SecurityOperator within 24 hours and a mandatory expiry, so an Organization with no SecurityOperator cannot create one directly. NOT RETROACTIVE: `protected_role?` governs the GRANT path, not the USE path, and `policy.entitlement.manage` is not materialized in `CAPABILITIES`, so no existing Assignment or authorization decision changes.

open_decisions.title: `write_observer_spec` does not exercise the production hook it claims to prove, and `GovernedWriteSentinel` has no suite-end non-vacuity check
open_decisions.authority: Round-19 architecture finding R19-ARCH-1 (ADR-137)
open_decisions.note: Eight of the file's ten examples build their own anonymous module and stand-in base class and never touch `GovernedWriteSentinel::Instrumentation`. MEASURED: replacing the production `Instrumentation#exec_params` body with a bare `super` -- so it observes nothing -- leaves `spec/architecture/write_observer_spec.rb` at 10 examples, 0 failures. NON-BLOCKING because the instrument IS bound: the same gutted hook fails `spec/acceptance/wf005_closed_fact_set_spec.rb` 7/7, and `complete_test_suite` is a mandatory manifest gate. What is wrong is the gate file's own header, which claims to be what binds it. SECOND HALF, AND THE MORE IMPORTANT ONE: unlike `AuthoritySentinel.assert_observed!`, `GovernedWriteSentinel` has NO `after(:suite)` non-vacuity check, so blinding it makes the run GREENER rather than failing it. REPAIR: point at least one example at `PG::Connection` with `Instrumentation` prepended, and add a suite-end `census.empty? -> raise` guard mirroring `assert_observed!`. RESOLVED 2026-08-10. BOTH HALVES, AND THE MEASUREMENT IN THIS NOTE WAS REPRODUCED FIRST: with `Instrumentation#exec_params` replaced by a bare `super`, `write_observer_spec.rb` was 10 examples / 0 failures and `wf005_closed_fact_set_spec.rb` was 7/7 red, exactly as recorded. FIRST HALF: the file now has a 'the production hook, on the real door' group that asserts `Instrumentation` is in `PG::Connection`'s ancestry AHEAD of the class, and drives a real statement naming a catalogue-derived governed table through a real `PG::Connection`, then reads the census back. That example fails on its own expectation against the gutted hook, which is the property the file's header used to claim and no example held. The census entry it makes is `reachable=false` and is restored after the example, so it cannot supply the evidence the suite-end judgement looks for. SECOND HALF, THE MORE IMPORTANT ONE: `GovernedWriteSentinel.assert_observed!` now refuses an empty census, and `after(:suite)` calls it on full-suite runs only, in the same shape and for the same reason `AuthoritySentinel` has at :427. It is callable so it is proved directly, and it is. The header no longer claims the stand-in examples bind the instrument; it states what each half proves and records that the acceptance spec was what bound it. Full suite 2964/0 with the guard live, so the census is non-empty on a real run and the guard is not merely inert.

open_decisions.title: `RaceHarness.open_connection` opens a raw unbounded connection, contradicting `PgTestConnection`'s own docstring
open_decisions.authority: Round-19 concurrency finding R19-CONC-6 (ADR-137)
open_decisions.note: MEASURED: `DbInspector` connections carry `statement_timeout = 15s`; `RaceHarness.open_connection` (`spec/support/race_harness.rb:196`) uses a bare `PG.connect` and carries `statement_timeout = 0`. That is the exact defect `spec/support/pg_test_connection.rb` was written to remove, and its docstring's claim to be 'the one place the suite opens a RAW PostgreSQL connection' is false. Three waits in `wf005_authority_lock_order_spec.rb` run on these connections with no bound of any kind (`pg_advisory_lock` at :130, `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` at :276 and :563). NON-BLOCKING: each contends only with rows its own example just created, and no hang could be demonstrated. REPAIR: `RaceHarness.open_connection` should route through `PgTestConnection.connect(user: DbInspector.superuser)`. RELATED AND NOW CLOSED: the 'deliberately unbounded' lock-order probe setup that BUILD_STATE carried as live exposure is in fact bounded by the 15s `statement_timeout` -- measured at 17.28s to `PG::QueryCanceled` with a complete residue report. It degrades to a failing example, never a hang, and is NOT a stability violation. RESOLVED 2026-08-09. `RaceHarness.open_connection` now returns `PgTestConnection.connect(user: DbInspector.superuser)`, so it carries `database.yml`'s own value rather than the server default, and `pg_test_connection.rb`'s claim to be 'the one place the suite opens a RAW PostgreSQL connection' is true again. THE BOUND DOES NOT DISARM THE HARNESS, which is why the FU-15 exemption for this file no longer applies: `database.yml` declares `statement_timeout` ALONE and no `lock_timeout`, so a gated operation still blocks on a contended lock - it simply cannot block for ever - and `RaceHarness::TIMEOUT_SECONDS` is already the same 15 seconds, so no wait here was ever designed to outlast it. The connections opened here are the lock HOLDERS, whose statements are uncontended; the waiters run on the ActiveRecord pool and were already bounded. PINNED BY 1 EXAMPLE in spec/architecture/test_harness_connection_bounds_spec.rb asserting a RaceHarness connection carries the SAME timeout DbInspector's does, not merely some timeout; and `race_harness.rb` was removed from that file's raw-connect exemption list, so a re-raw'd connection fails the run rather than being tolerated by name. `scheduled_action_harness.rb` remains exempt and is NOT claimed to be fixed.

open_decisions.title: PROOF 264 measures the lock order at one of the three protected writes
open_decisions.authority: Round-19 concurrency finding R19-CONC-1 (ADR-137)
open_decisions.note: PROOF 264 drives only `QueueCrawl`, and `blocks_on_held_grant?` only drives `CrawlStore#insert_crawl`. The order at `cancel` and `activate_version` is ASSUMED -- this tranche's own declared defect class, and the one round 16 was called for. The concurrency lens measured all three from both ends with `pg_blocking_pids` and the order HOLDS everywhere, so this is NON-BLOCKING. But it holds as a property of the PLANNER (materialized-CTE / InitPlan evaluation order), not of anything enforced, and in `crawl_policy_store.rb:120` the two EXISTS sit in one CTE where `order_qual_clauses` sorts by estimated cost. REPAIR: run PROOF 264's measurement at all three writes using the `WRITES` battery shape `wf005_grant_battery_spec.rb` already establishes. RESOLVED 2026-08-10 (ADR-147) BY THE MEASUREMENT THIS NOTE ASKED FOR, at all three writes. `spec/acceptance/wf005_lock_order_all_writes_spec.rb` runs PROOF 264's measurement -- hold the grant row, start the write, wait until it is blocked behind the holder, then require a third connection to FAIL to take `organizations` FOR NO KEY UPDATE -- against every DISTINCT write in `ProtectedWrites.covered`, the registry FU-61's completeness gate proves against the repository, so a fourth write is measured the day it is registered instead of inheriting this proof. PROOF 264's advisory-lock scaffolding is gone: it existed to get the HANDLER blocked at a known point, and driving the STORE directly needs none. MEASURED: the order HOLDS at all three, including `CrawlPolicyStore#activate_version`, whose two EXISTS sit in one CTE where `order_qual_clauses` sorts by estimated cost -- which is worth more now than when this note was written, because FU-58 has just added a conjunct to that CTE and the note predicted exactly that kind of change would move the estimate. NOT CLAIMED: this measures the order at the writes as they are planned TODAY. It is a gate against a future reordering, not a proof that the planner cannot reorder.

open_decisions.title: The protected-grant limb has NO counterpart at any protected write, and the safety of that is a caller census
open_decisions.authority: Round-19 adversarial finding R-ADV-1 (ADR-138)
open_decisions.note: The three protected writes never read `protected_permission_allowlist` or `bootstrap_admin_exception` for ANY capability. `confers?`'s `return true unless PROTECTED.key?` is a property of the RUBY evaluator and has no analogue in the SQL, so the stores' comment 'this is the baseline CARRIED' is inaccurate: what is carried is the baseline MINUS its protected limb. MEASURED at `CrawlStartStore#cancel` with an ordinary OrganizationAdmin grant and capability `role.manage`: Ruby `authorize` DENIES (`missing_authority`, granting=0) while the write returns `capability_authorized=true, moved=1` and irreversibly cancels a running Crawl. LATENT, not live: no production caller passes a protected capability to these writes, and `CAPABILITIES.fetch` raises KeyError for 13 of the 15 PROTECTED keys, so the exposed surface is exactly `role.manage` and `invitation.approve` — the two keys in both tables. BUT the safety rests on a CALLER CENSUS, which is the 'one deletion away from nothing' shape FU-48 exists to remove, and the census is wider than recorded: `WriteAuthority.for` has FOUR call sites in app/, not three — the three handlers plus `app/workflows/wf005/authority_attestation.rb:66`, reached through `PostWaitDecision#authority_attestation`. Both `attest` and `authority_attestation` take a free `capability:` parameter. REPAIR OPTIONS: carry a `protected_permitted` boolean derived from `PROTECTED.key?(capability)` the way `read_only_permitted` already carries the sixth column, with the allowlist bound when it is true; or refuse at the builder — `WriteAuthority.for` raises for a capability in PROTECTED until the limb is carried, which turns the census into an enforced invariant. The second is smaller and fails closed. RESOLVED 2026-08-10 (ADR-147). THE LIMB IS CARRIED, NOT FENCED. `WriteAuthority` gains a `protected_capability` boolean derived once from `PROTECTED.key?(capability)` -- the same shape `read_only_permitted` already has for the sixth column -- and all three capability CTEs bind `AND (NOT $n::boolean OR ra.bootstrap_admin_exception OR ra.protected_permission_allowlist @> to_jsonb($m::text))`, which is `confers?`'s protected limb exactly. THE BUILDER-REFUSAL OPTION THIS NOTE PREFERRED WAS NOT TAKEN, and the reason is that it makes the defect UNPROVABLE: if `WriteAuthority.for` raises for a PROTECTED capability, nothing can drive the statement with one to show it refuses, and the next protected write inherits the same gap. THIS NOTE'S OWN MEASUREMENT IS CORRECTED. It reads 'Ruby `authorize` DENIES (`missing_authority`, granting=0)'. Driven today, `authorize` ALLOWS for a bootstrapped actor, because it aggregates over EVERY effective Assignment and the WF-001 bootstrap grant carries `bootstrap_admin_exception`, which `confers?` accepts. THE DIVERGENCE IS PER GRANT, NOT PER ACTOR, which is the level the write works at: it re-reads the grants the decision relied on. Proved that way -- an ordinary OrganizationAdmin Assignment with an empty allowlist and no exception, for which `protected_grant?` is false, was authorized by the write and cancelled a running Crawl. THREE EXAMPLES, NOT ONE: the refusal, the ADMISSION once :314's approved allowlist carries the capability (a blanket denial would pass the first and make the allowlist meaningless), and a non-protected capability still admitted (a limb keyed on an empty allowlist would break every production cancellation). The exposed surface is DERIVED rather than transcribed: the intersection of `CAPABILITIES` and `PROTECTED` is asserted to be exactly `role.manage` and `invitation.approve`, and every other PROTECTED key is required to raise KeyError from `CAPABILITIES.fetch`. MEASURED AGAINST THE TRUE PRE-CHANGE CODE -- limb and both parameters removed together, because removing the conjunct alone makes PostgreSQL reject the bind and produces a crash rather than a failed expectation -- exactly one example fails, on its own assertion.

open_decisions.title: `f1_role_assignments_lifecycle_guard` is BEFORE UPDATE only; an INSERT may mint an active grant with any protected allowlist
open_decisions.authority: Round-19 adversarial finding R-ADV-3 (ADR-138)
open_decisions.note: The only trigger on `role_assignments` is `role_assignments_lifecycle_guard BEFORE UPDATE FOR EACH ROW`. There is NO INSERT trigger and NO DELETE trigger, and the only CHECK touching the allowlist for a non-pending row is the 30-day expiry rule (`role_assignment_pending_has_no_allowlist` is `status <> 'pending' OR ...`). So an INSERT may create a row with `status='active'`, any allowlist including all 15 PROTECTED keys, and `bootstrap_admin_exception=true`, bounded only by `bootstrap_exception_is_admin` and the one-per-org partial unique index. `RoleAssignmentStore#insert` takes both as free parameters and its sole caller hardcodes `[]`. CONTAINED TODAY: `f1_runtime` holds INSERT/SELECT/UPDATE but NOT DELETE, and no `f1_*` role is superuser or bypassrls, so delete-and-reinsert, `session_replication_role` and `DISABLE TRIGGER` are all unavailable. DOES NOT REACH THE PROTECTED WRITES: an INSERT mints a new id and the capability CTE joins on the CARRIED `g.id = ra.id AND g.state_version = ra.state_version`; the `pending -> active` route cannot apply either, because `effective_role_assignments` selects `status='active'` only and the transition bumps `state_version`. WHY IT IS RECORDED ANYWAY: round 19 cited this guard as an INDEPENDENT ground for the safety of the unbound protected limb, and it is not one — dual control at INSERT time is enforced in Ruby alone. REPAIR: extend the guard to BEFORE INSERT for the allowlist and bootstrap columns, or add a CHECK that an inserted active row carries an empty allowlist unless the bootstrap exception applies. RESOLVED 2026-08-09 by migration 20260809100000, which adds `role_assignments_insert_guard BEFORE INSERT FOR EACH ROW` running `f1_role_assignments_insert_guard()`. THE RULE ENFORCED IS THE ONE THE UPDATE GUARD ALREADY STATES, applied to the operation that was missing it: the approved protected authority is written EXACTLY ONCE, by the `pending -> active` transition, so a row cannot be born holding it. It refuses any INSERT whose `protected_permission_allowlist` is non-empty, at every status. IT HAD TO BE A TRIGGER, not the CHECK this record offered as an alternative: a CHECK cannot distinguish INSERT from UPDATE, so a CHECK strong enough to close this would also forbid the ratified activation. NO RATIFIED PATH IS NARROWED - WF-001's genesis OrganizationAdmin and every WF-013 insert already write `[]`, and `RoleAssignmentStore#activate` still writes the allowlist on the edge that may. `bootstrap_admin_exception` is NOT additionally guarded at insert: it remains bounded by `bootstrap_exception_is_admin` and the one-per-org partial unique index, which is the ratified genesis path, and that is not claimed as new. FIXTURE CONSEQUENCE, DISCLOSED: `TenantSeeder.create_role_assignment` previously INSERTED active grants holding allowlists directly, which the guard now refuses. It was changed to seed through the same `pending -> active` edge the product uses, so a seeded protected grant now has the same history as a granted one - a stronger fixture, not a workaround. Two acceptance examples changed as a direct consequence and both are recorded rather than quietly adjusted: the 30-day protected-expiry CHECK is now proved on the ACTIVATION edge, because that is the only moment an allowlist can legally arrive; and a `rejected` Assignment carrying protected authority is now UNREACHABLE by construction, so 'confers nothing in any inactive state' covers `revoked` and `expired`, and a separate example asserts that a rejected grant has no way to hold protected authority at all - which is stronger than the authorizer declining to honour one. PINNED BY 2 EXAMPLES in spec/acceptance/wf013_role_assignment_invariants_spec.rb, verified by dropping the trigger from f1_test: with it gone, an `active` grant carrying `role.manage` inserts with nothing raised. `pending` is deliberately excluded from that loop so the pre-existing `role_assignment_pending_has_no_allowlist` CHECK cannot stand in for the trigger.

open_decisions.title: `AuthorityFixture` carries second copies of BOTH write-authority derivations, and nothing binds them to the production builder
open_decisions.authority: Round-19 final-gate adversarial finding A-1 (ADR-138)
open_decisions.note: `spec/support/authority_fixture.rb:31-32` computes `CAPABILITIES.fetch(capability)` and `READ_ONLY_CAPABILITIES.include?(capability)` independently of `IdentityAccess::Authorization::WriteAuthority.for`. THIS IS THE MECHANISM THAT HID R-ADV-2: because every battery case built its authority through the fixture, all of them proved what the STATEMENT does with a correct value and none proved the value was derived, which is how three capability-scoped mutations survived 1185 acceptance examples. The round-19 repair routes the two new cases around the fixture via `production_authority`, so the LIVE gap is closed, but the duplicate expressions remain and NOTHING ASSERTS THEY AGREE — `grep -rn AuthorityFixture spec/architecture/` returns nothing. They are textually identical today, so there is no live divergence; the exposure is future drift. If `WriteAuthority.for` gains a third input or changes a derivation, every fixture-built case keeps proving the old shape while production uses the new one, silently. REPAIR: the fixture's DEFAULTS should come from the production builder, with explicit overrides retained for the deliberately-wrong authorities the negative proofs need (that capability is the fixture's stated purpose and must not be removed). A one-example architecture gate asserting that `AuthorityFixture.build` with no overrides equals `WriteAuthority.for` on `allowed_roles` and `read_only_permitted` for EVERY materialized capability would convert the assumption into a control, in the shape `permission_baseline_transcription_spec.rb` already establishes. MEASURED at round 20 (finding F-4), both directions, one capability at a time: breaking the PRODUCTION derivation dies at exactly the affected write for all SIX capability/expression pairs (ADR-138 verified three of the six; the other three also hold). In the fixture direction, a permissive drift of its `read_only_permitted` copy fails LOUD (3 failures, one per write), while a permissive drift of its `allowed_roles` copy changes NO verdict — it is invisible and simultaneously load-bearing for nothing, because the one case needing a restrictive cell passes `allowed_roles: %w[NoSuchRole]` explicitly and a union still contains the actor's role so the COMMIT control still commits. So the duplication CANNOT be made to hide a real defect today; the exposure is purely future drift, in a case written later against the fixture default. ROUND-20 EXTENSION (finding F4): the fixture diverges from production in SELECTION as well as in derivation, which this note did not record. `AuthorityFixture.active_grants` selects a WIDER set than `AuthorizationStore#effective_role_assignments` — measured 1 row vs 0 for an active-but-not-yet-effective grant — and applies no `confers?` filter at all. It also orders `grant_ids` by `ORDER BY id` while production takes whatever order `effective_role_assignments` returns, which carries NO `ORDER BY`; `same_principal?` compares those arrays with `==`. Neither is reachable, because a write's authority and its attestation are built from the same `Decision` object, but a fixture that selects differently from production is the same hazard class as one that derives differently, and the repair should cover both. RESOLVED 2026-08-10. THE DUPLICATION IS REMOVED RATHER THAN GATED. `AuthorityFixture.build` now constructs an `AuthenticatedActor` and a `Decision` and calls `IdentityAccess::Authorization::WriteAuthority.for`, so the two derivations this note names have ONE copy and it is production's; `allowed_roles` survives as an override applied AFTER the production build, because the negative proofs need a deliberately wrong cell. THE SELECTION LIMB TOO: `active_grants` now runs `AuthorizationStore#effective_role_assignments` instead of a second SELECT, with the Organization restriction applied explicitly because `DbInspector.connection` is the BYPASSRLS superuser and the FORCE RLS that scopes production's query is not in force on it. MEASURED, BOTH DIRECTIONS, AND THEY ARE NOT THE SAME STRENGTH. The SELECTION change is behavioural and revert-proved: restoring the old `status = 'active'` predicate inside the new signature fails `spec/architecture/authority_fixture_binding_spec.rb` on its own expectation, reproducing this note's 1-row-against-0 measurement for an active-but-not-yet-effective grant. The DERIVATION change cannot be revert-proved behaviourally and this record will not claim it was: the two expressions were textually identical, so restoring the copy leaves every behavioural example green. It is held STRUCTURALLY instead, by an example asserting the fixture names neither baseline constant and does not call `WriteAuthority.new` — which does fail on revert, on its own expectation. The agreement gate the earlier note proposed is present and is wider than proposed (EVERY member of the `Data` object at EVERY materialized capability, not `allowed_roles` and `read_only_permitted` alone, because a member added later and derived only in production would satisfy the narrower gate and diverge). All 159 examples across the seven fixture-consuming spec files were green before and after, so no consumer's behaviour moved. WHAT IS NOT CLOSED, NAMED: the `confers?` filter. Production applies it inside `authorize` through a predicate private to `CommandAuthorizer`, and the fixture deliberately does not, because building the authority a deleted or wrong `confers?` produces upstream is what several negative proofs ARE. And `now`: production takes it from the command's clock and a fixture has no command, so the default is the process clock and a caller proving a time-dependent property must pass its own. Both are stated in the fixture's own header rather than left to be discovered.

open_decisions.title: Nothing enforces the completeness of the battery's `WRITES` set, on which the round-19 repair's structural claim depends
open_decisions.authority: Round-19 final-gate adversarial finding A-2 (ADR-138)
open_decisions.note: `spec/acceptance/wf005_grant_battery_spec.rb:56` declares `WRITES` as a hand-maintained literal, and the only thing referencing it is the `WRITES.each` at :447. The round-19 repair's claim to be STRUCTURAL rather than three more proofs rests entirely on inheritance: twelve shared examples run at every entry in that map. A FOURTH PROTECTED WRITE WOULD INHERIT NONE OF THEM and no gate would say so. Completeness was established this round by the architecture lens planning all 391 SQL statements in app/ and lib/ through `EXPLAIN (GENERIC_PLAN)` and collecting `ModifyTable` nodes — exactly six statements modify `crawls`/`crawl_policies`, the three human-authorized ones carry `WriteAuthority` and the three service ones (`start`, `fail`, `terminalize`) have no human path because neither caller ever calls `authenticate`. But that was a REVIEW ACTIVITY, not a gate, and it does not run again. REPAIR: an architecture spec that derives the protected-write set from the repository as EVERY STATEMENT CARRYING A `capability_authority` CTE, and fails when it is not exactly the set `WRITES` enumerates. AN EARLIER DRAFT OF THIS NOTE ALSO OFFERED 'every store method taking an `authority:` parameter', AND THAT DERIVATION IS WRONG: measured, only `CrawlStartStore#cancel` takes it as a keyword; `insert_crawl` and `activate_version` receive it inside a row Hash via `row.fetch(:authority)`, and a `[:authority]` grep additionally matches an unrelated WF-013 ledger column at `role_assignment_store.rb:131`. A gate written to that spec would cover 1 of 3 and PASS — this tranche's own defect class inside the repair for it. The CTE derivation is exact repo-wide: 3 of 3, zero false positives, and `epoch_authority` cross-checks to the same set. That removes the class rather than the instance, which is the standard ADR-095 and the round-15 A15-1 repair both set. PRIORITY, MEASURED: `crawl.recover` is ratified in WORKFLOW_SPECIFICATIONS.md's WF-005 Recovery Path and is NOT in `PermissionBaseline::CAPABILITIES`, so a fourth protected write is SCHEDULED WORK rather than a hypothesis, and the gate should exist before it lands. RESOLVED 2026-08-10. THE CTE DERIVATION IS THE ONE THIS NOTE ALREADY MEASURED AS EXACT, and the `authority:`-parameter derivation it warned against is not used. Four checks: the set comparison; a non-vacuity check that every occurrence of the marker in the corpus landed in a definition, so a derivation that came back short fails instead of passing; the `epoch_authority` cross-check, which this note records agreeing and which now runs; and a check that each registered identity names a class and method Ruby can resolve. open_decisions.title: Staged response bodies are held on F-02 rather than in the canonical `stored_objects` blob store
open_decisions.authority: DECISIONS ADR-143 part 3 (S-07-010)
open_decisions.note: WORKFLOW_SPECIFICATIONS.md :462 requires staged body bytes that are "immutable and inaccessible to product reads"; :464 destroys the "separate staging reference" at success and :466 at 24 hours. The canonical home is `stored_objects` (POSTGRESQL_SCHEMA.md :231), a shared platform table with `storage_provider CHECK ('aws_s3')`, six lifecycle states, KMS key references and an encryption-context digest. IT HAS NEVER BEEN BUILT, no S-07 tranche owns it, and standing it up requires an external paid provider — which AUTONOMY_POLICY makes an OWNER decision, not an implementer's. S-07-010 therefore stages through F-02, which supplies all three ratified properties through a frozen public contract this repository already uses for the same purpose (S-05's redacted verification payload), with the AAD purpose `temporary_processing` — the retention class SCORE_EVIDENCE_MODEL.md names for staging bytes. CORRECTED 2026-08-07 BY THE INDEPENDENT REVIEW (R1-3): this note previously claimed "both destruction points are proved", and that was FALSE. :464's success-path destruction is implemented and proved; :466's "then destroys them" at the 24-hour bound is NOT implemented, is not this tranche's — MTX-008 retention says the window is "owned by 015 DATA_LIFECYCLE.md" and FOUNDATION-003 excludes the retention executor from F-03 — and is now carried as FU-69 instead of being absorbed by a sentence in this one. What S-07-010 does own and does enforce is the REFUSAL at the bound, which fails closed and is proved by PROOF 174. open_decisions.title: Accepted WF-005 events omit the `prior_aggregate_version` / `committed_aggregate_version` base members
open_decisions.authority: DECISIONS ADR-143 (S-07-010, contract self-review against API_CONTRACTS.md :938)
open_decisions.note: API_CONTRACTS.md § Closed profile payloads makes `prior_aggregate_version` and `committed_aggregate_version` BASE MEMBERS of every `created` and `state_transition` payload (`created`: "prior_aggregate_version: null, committed_aggregate_version: uint53"; `state_transition`: "prior... uint53, committed... uint53; committed version equals root aggregate version and prior is lower"). `Handlers::QueueCrawl`'s `CrawlQueued` and `Handlers::CompleteCrawl`'s terminal envelope carry NEITHER, and `CrawlQueued` also omits `from_state`/`to_state` as base members while carrying an ad hoc `state`. The S-07-010 events (`DocumentDiscovered`, `IngestionQueued`, `IngestionStarted`, `DocumentIngested`, `IngestionSucceeded`, `IngestionFailed`, `IngestionDeadLettered`) carry all of them, so the corpus is now inconsistent with itself. NOT REPAIRED HERE because the divergent events belong to ACCEPTED tranches (S-07-002, S-07-009) and changing an accepted event payload is a contract change rather than an implementation choice. Same class as FU-33, which records `CrawlQueued`/`CrawlStarted` omitting `accepted_document_count` from the same table; a single repair should close both. MEASURED 2026-08-10 AND NOT REPAIRED. See FU-33, which now carries the member-level delta for all of them so the decision is one reading rather than an investigation. In short: the TERMINAL envelope in `Handlers::CompleteCrawl` is the small case this note describes — it is missing `prior_aggregate_version` and `committed_aggregate_version` and carries one member the profile does not admit (`crawl_id`, which duplicates the event row's own aggregate id) — while `CrawlQueued` and `CrawlStarted` are wholesale non-conformant in BOTH directions. So this note's framing, that they 'omit the base members', is right for the terminal envelope and understates the other two. The reason for stopping is unchanged and is now better supported: bringing them into conformance DELETES payload members from accepted tranches, including two the accepted block added for CAP-007 observability, which is a contract decision rather than an implementation choice. RESOLVED 2026-08-10 BY OWNER DECISION (ADR-146), together with FU-33 as both notes said it should be. `prior_aggregate_version` and `committed_aggregate_version` are now emitted by every WF-005 Crawl-aggregate event: null/0 for `CrawlQueued` under the `created` profile, and `new_version - 1` / `new_version` for each `state_transition`, which is :938's 'committed version equals root aggregate version and prior is lower' rather than a second derivation of the version. `CrawlQueued`'s ad hoc `state` is replaced by the base `from_state`/`to_state` pair, and the terminal envelope's `crawl_id` -- which duplicated the root `affected_entity_id` -- is gone. THE MEMBERS THAT LOOK LIKE SURPLUS AND ARE NOT: `project_id`, `reason_code` and `outcome` STAY, because :703 puts all three on the event ROOT and the flat ledger builder reads them out of the same hash. THE BROADER FINDING IS FU-74: :703 also makes `event_payload` a NESTED object and no emitter in this repository nests it.
