open_decisions.title: :466's 24-hour DESTRUCTION of retained staging bytes has no executor
open_decisions.authority: S-07-010 independent review, finding R1-3; WORKFLOW_SPECIFICATIONS.md :466; contracts/S-07.json MTX-008 retention
open_decisions.note: :466 puts TWO obligations on staged bytes after a failure: "retains inaccessible staging bytes for AT MOST 24 HOURS from fetch completion, THEN DESTROYS THEM; a replay after destruction is `staged_body_missing`". S-07-010 implements the REFUSAL — `staging_expires_at` is stamped once, frozen by the guard, and checked before the bytes are read, so a worker arriving after the window refuses rather than ingesting (PROOF 174) — and implements the success-path destruction (:464's "deletes the separate staging reference", PROOF 169). NOTHING DESTROYS THE BYTES AT THE BOUND. A `dead_letter` job's staged ciphertext is retained indefinitely: `Platform::Encryption.erase` has exactly one ingestion caller and it is on the success path. WHY IT IS NOT REPAIRED IN S-07-010: MTX-008 retention states the window is "owned by 015 DATA_LIFECYCLE.md", FOUNDATION-003 excludes the retention/deletion executor from F-03, and BACKGROUND_PROCESSING's action catalogue is CLOSED — the plausible kinds (`staged_object_invariant_sweep_due`, `lifecycle_deletion_*`) belong to the lifecycle and maintenance surfaces that no S-07 tranche owns. THE EXPOSURE, STATED: encrypted customer page bytes are retained past a bound the contract sets, behind a capability with no product read path. It is a retention-policy breach rather than a disclosure, and the refusal above means no workflow can consume them. MUST BE RESOLVED by whoever builds the retention executor, and before any customer-facing retention claim is made about crawl staging.

open_decisions.title: Catalog v1 measures AI PRESENCE and CITATION; nothing in it checks whether an AI stated something FALSE about a business
open_decisions.authority: OD-010 ratified check-catalog-v1 (seven Definitions); SCORE_EVIDENCE_MODEL.md CHK-AIP-001; probe evidence in operations/probe-harness/evidence/runs.jsonl
open_decisions.note: The commercial framing of the product is Missing, Losing and Wrong. `check-catalog-v1` covers the first two and NOT the third. CHK-AIP-001 measures whether a business is named, cited and entity-identified for a frozen intent set — that is MISSING — and competitor visibility in the same observation supports LOSING. NOTHING IN THE RATIFIED CATALOGUE EVALUATES THE TRUTH OF WHAT A MACHINE SAID. The probe evidence makes the gap concrete rather than theoretical: `runs.jsonl` records `credentials_attributed_by_machines`, `people_attributed_by_machines` and `locations_attributed_by_machines` per business, and the 2026-08-07 export carries a `claims_a_human_must_check` list plus the caveat that in run 01 fourteen candidate errors were chased and five survived verification against the business's own site or a public register. Those five are exactly the Wrong case: a machine stating a licence number, a director or an address that the register contradicts. WHAT MUST NOT HAPPEN, AND HAS NOT: CHK-TR-001 must not be broadened to absorb accuracy — it measures whether published Organization structured data matches the frozen public identity, which is a statement about the SITE, not about what a model said. No eighth Definition is added, because OD-010 ratified exactly seven and 'the catalogue is not broadened by this ratification'. No accuracy semantics are slipped into an existing outcome code. WHAT IS OWED: a future catalogue version, approved by its own owner decision, carrying an accuracy Definition with its own subject, evidence schema, ground-truth source, outcome codes, impact mapping and — the hard part — a defensible rule for what counts as ground truth, since a public register and a business's own site can themselves disagree. Until that exists the product measures presence and says so; it does not claim to detect misinformation.

open_decisions.title: Neither Project-creation form can assert a local presence, so every Project a human creates through the UI declares it INAPPLICABLE
open_decisions.authority: WORKFLOW_SPECIFICATIONS.md :621, :657; SCORE_EVIDENCE_MODEL.md :273, :587; API_CONTRACTS.md :371 `LocalBusinessProfile`, :408 ATTR-BootstrapOrganization; measured against the development database 2026-08-09
open_decisions.note: WHAT IS BUILT: WF-001 now takes the ratified `first_project: object<ProjectProfile>` body :408 names and :621 requires, validates it through WF-002's OWN shared validator so the two Project-creation paths cannot drift, and commits the genesis Project's full creation profile including `profile_attesting_account_id` (the first OrganizationAdmin, created in the same transaction) and `profile_committed_at`. BOTH branches work at the command layer and are pinned: applicability false with a 20-500 reason, and applicability true with a complete `local-business-profile-v1` whose business name must equal the exact normalized Organization display name. MEASURED, NOT ARGUED: before this, 16 of 18 development Projects carried the all-NULL profile shape - legal under `projects_local_profile_shape`, but not a valid false - so `CHK-LP-001` returned `error / local_profiles_absent / input_evidence_missing` and Local Presence blocked the score BY OMISSION. It now returns `not_applicable / local_presence_not_applicable`, pinned end to end in spec/acceptance/wf007_evaluation_spec.rb over a real crawl. WHAT IS OWED: NEITHER FORM CAN ASSERT A LOCAL PRESENCE. `/start/bootstrap-organization` (WEB-003) and the WF-002 project screen both hard-code `local_presence_applicable=false` and ask only for the reason, because the true branch needs a `local-business-profile-v1` form that has never been built - address_text, telephone_e164 and service_areas, with business_name fixed to the Organization display name so it is not asked. THE CONSEQUENCE IS CUSTOMER-VISIBLE: a business that DOES trade from premises can only register by declaring, in its own words, that it does not, and `CHK-LP-001` then returns `not_applicable` for a business that should be measured. The reason text is genuinely the registrant's; the APPLICABILITY answer is not offered. WHAT MUST NOT HAPPEN, AND HAS NOT: no implementer derives applicability from the presence or absence of an address, auto-generates the reason text, or relaxes `Applicability#local_presence_entry`, which correctly treats an absent or reasonless profile as NO decision rather than as a false one -- :587 requires an OrganizationAdmin or MarketingOperator to record the reason, and silence is not a `false`. THE FIX IS A FORM, NOT A CONTRACT CHANGE: the command, handler, validator, store and CHECK constraint all already accept the true branch. RESOLVED 2026-08-09. Both screens now ask the applicability question and offer both branches, through one shared `LocalPresenceForm` controller concern and one shared `shared/_local_presence_fields` partial, for the same reason both paths already share `Workflows::Wf002::ProjectCreation`: two screens asking the same ratified question must not drift into asking it two ways. Every field predicate delegates to that shared validator rather than restating its rule. The Local Business Profile's `business_name` is never a control: WEB-003 uses the Organization name typed one control above, and WEB-012 reads it on its own authorized connection through QRY-001, which discloses nothing QRY-001 does not already disclose. `service_areas` is entered one per line in any order and sorted by UTF-8 bytes before submission - transport normalization of the same kind as NFC and trimming, adding no area and removing none; a duplicate or oversized member is NOT dropped but returned as a field error. THE THREE PROHIBITIONS STILL HOLD, AND ARE NOW STRUCTURAL: applicability is not derived from whether an address is present; the reason text is not composed, defaulted or suggested; `Applicability#local_presence_entry` is untouched. NEITHER RADIO IS PRESELECTED, and an unanswered form carries applicability `nil` all the way to the workflow, which refuses it as `project_local_applicability_invalid` - so silence cannot become a `false` even for a caller that skips the field check. PINNED BY 5 EXAMPLES in spec/requests/registration_access_flow_spec.rb, each verified to fail on its own assertion when the change is reverted; the sharpest is that under the old code an unanswered form returned 303 and CREATED a Project declaring inapplicability. NOT DONE, AND NOT CLAIMED: the 16 development Projects carrying the all-NULL shape are still not backfilled (:587 requires a human to record each reason), and no ratified artifact was edited.

open_decisions.title: CHK-TI-001 stays indeterminate on any site that links to a same-host non-HTML asset, over a crawl whose coverage is full
open_decisions.authority: WORKFLOW_SPECIFICATIONS.md :452, :478; SCORE_EVIDENCE_MODEL.md :294; S-07-007 in-crawl link discovery; measured against the live xirconhomes.com.au crawl 2026-08-08
open_decisions.note: S-07-007's in-crawl link discovery is BUILT: the crawl now follows the links its pages name, and CHK-TI-001 reaches passed/internal_links_resolve whenever every in-scope target is an HTML page (pinned in spec/acceptance/wf007_evaluation_spec.rb). open_decisions.title: The event ROOT envelope is non-conformant across every emitter, in both directions
open_decisions.authority: Measured 2026-08-10 while taking FU-33/FU-67 (ADR-146); not decided by the owner's conformance decision, which was about the closed PROFILE
open_decisions.note: API_CONTRACTS.md :703 makes `event_payload: object<EventProfilePayload>` a NESTED member of the event root and enumerates the root's exact members.
